arguments.premise_synthesis: A Charles Schwab study over 80 twenty-year periods compared hypothetical investors: Peter (perfect timer), Ashley (lump sum), Matthew (dollar-cost averaging), Rosie (poor timer), and Larry (cash). The study found that any form of investing, even poor timing, significantly outperforms staying in cash. Additionally, a chart study dating back to 1988 showed that investing only on days when the market makes new all-time highs produces better returns than investing on random days. The worst performance came from keeping money in cash, reinforcing that any investment strategy beats cash.
arguments.conclusion_supported: Historical evidence shows that long-term investors who stay invested, regardless of timing, outperform those who hold cash, and that investing at market highs does not harm returns.
